title: Nabataean Petra links caravan routes
summary: Petra developed as a Nabataean centre connecting routes between Arabia, Egypt and Syria. Rock-cut monuments and water storage systems reveal how a substantial settlement operated in an arid landscape.

claims.text: Petra developed as a Nabataean centre connecting routes between Arabia, Egypt and Syria. Rock-cut monuments and water storage systems reveal how a substantial settlement operated in an arid landscape.
Fourth century BCE–first century CE is a broad Nabataean context, not all habitation.

The city links environmental engineering with long-distance exchange. Architectural similarities alone cannot identify every trade route; the cited overview supplies the evidence for Petra’s role as a caravan centre.
